title: Resolve DB0-only vs multi-database SELECT by cluster policy
intent: Checks the answer correctly separates clustered/geo/CRDB database-0-only behavior from non-clustered multi-database behavior, rejecting the blanket always-DB0 assumption, and steers to key prefixes.
prompt: A team assumed Azure Managed Redis always supports 16 logical databases and used SELECT across them. Review the design against the deployment's cluster policy and correct it.

input_artifacts.name: db-usage.txt
input_artifacts.content: deployment: two environments, one clustered (also used for geo), one non-clustered; app calls SELECT 3 for sessions and SELECT 7 for jobs on both; assumption: 'AMR always has 16 databases everywhere'

embedded_defects.defect: Uses SELECT to non-zero databases on the clustered/geo deployment where only database 0 exists.
Applies a blanket always-DB0 or always-16-DB assumption instead of distinguishing the non-clustered policy that can expose multiple databases.
Relies on multiple databases instead of key prefixes for logical separation.
